covariate-definitions.name: Country income level
covariate-definitions.description: We conducted subgroup analysis based on geographic location, divided into four income groups (low, lower-middle, upper-middle, and high income) according to the World Bank’s country classification (World Bank Group 2021).

covariate-definitions.name: Intervention method category
covariate-definitions.description: We explored whether intervention effects varied depending on the intervention methods used at trial entry. Subgroup analysis was conducted based on the four intervention categories defined in the CSHP 2018 classification: synchronous video (2-way interaction), asynchronous content (provision of recorded health record, stored audio or video, etc.), remote patient monitoring (e.g., telemetry), and mobile health (using mobile devices).

covariate-definitions.name: Sensitivity analysis 1: overall risk of bias
covariate-definitions.description:
This covariate classifies studies based on their overall risk of bias judgement using the RoB 2 tool.

•	Low risk of bias: studies judged to be at low risk of bias across all domains.
•	Some concerns or high risk of bias: studies judged to have some concerns or high risk of bias in one or more domains.
values: Some concerns or high risk of bias

covariate-definitions.name: Sensitivity analysis 2: unit of analysis matches unit of allocation
covariate-definitions.description:
This covariate distinguishes studies in which the unit of analysis was consistent with the unit of allocation. Studies were included in the “Yes” category if the original publication reported either:
•	Analysis conducted at the cluster level, or
•	Individual-level analysis adjusted appropriately for clustering (e.g. using generalized estimating equations, mixed-effects models, or robust standard errors). Studies that did not account for clustering in the original analysis were assigned to the “No” category.
values: No (unit of analysis does not match unit of allocation)
Yes (unit of analysis matches unit of allocation)

covariate-definitions.name: Sensitivity analysis 3: imputation of missing outcome data
covariate-definitions.description:
This covariate distinguishes studies according to whether the original analysis included imputation for missing outcome data. Studies were categorised as:
•	No imputation: trials that reported either no missing data or used available case analysis without imputing values.
•	Imputation performed: trials that imputed missing outcome data using methods such as last observation carried forward (LOCF), baseline observation carried forward (BPCF), mean imputation, or multiple imputation.

covariate-definitions.name: Sensitivity analysis 4: validity of outcome measure
covariate-definitions.description:
This covariate categorises studies based on the validity of the outcome measure used for the outcome under analysis.
•	Validated outcome measure: studies that used a measurement tool with evidence of validity or reliability in the target population.
•	Non-validated outcome measure: studies that used a self-developed or unvalidated measurement tool without documented psychometric properties.

covariate-definitions.name: Single vs multiple telepharmacy approaches
covariate-definitions.description: We conducted subgroup analysis to examine whether the number of telepharmacy components influenced the treatment effect. Interventions were categorized as ‘single’ or ‘multiple’ approaches. The ‘multiple’ categories included interventions that combined two or more communication modes, even if delivered via the same device (e.g. phone calls and mobile app messages on a smartphone).
